RMNH259388b_ventral.scale_note: Naturalis cm bar code fit 69.1 (same bar as the dorsal frame; not individually zoom-verified)

RMNH259485b_dorsal.scale_note: TE263 ruler 0..180 mm baseline extent by code (te263_ends.py) = 88.61 px/cm, equals the tick fit

measured_naturalis_wings_CC0._note: CC0 spread wings with a verified ruler. Root = proximal 4 % along the root->tip axis (planform_stats.analyse root_mode='axis'); these preparations keep more shoulder/back-feather mass than the Slater wings, so root-to-tip L (16.7-17.3 cm) is not comparable with Slater L (15.7); single-wing area is (85-89 vs 85.5 cm2). Edge halo of the masks: 1-3 px (cream-background frames after tightening; 0.1-0.3 mm).

measured_study_skins._note: Straight study skins, neck fully extended: bill-tip to tail-tip 19.6-23.1 cm, longer than a live bird with a retracted neck. Tail often fanned (tail tip partly estimated). Wing front (shoulder proxy) is LOW confidence (+-40-100 px). Scale valid in the ruler plane only; the skin top sits 2-3 cm above it (a few % magnification). 5070087 has no ruler (cutting-mat grid presumed 1 cm, unverified). Per-image detail in derived/skin_candidates.json.

measured_feather_atlas_images._note: Image-measured per-feather vane length (vertical extent), max vane width (horizontal extent in any row, slightly over-reads tilted feathers) and area, left to right in the atlas layout. Scale: derived/atlas_scale_results.json; scripts atlas_scale.py, atlas_feathers.py. Table values (starling_records.json) are measured along the rachis and are the better length data.

crosschecks.slater_vs_naturalis_note: Single-wing AREA agrees across the two independent sources/scales (Slater 20907 male 85.5 dorsal / 91.1 ventral cm2; Naturalis male 85.2 dorsal (label hides part of the leading edge) / 86.8 ventral; Naturalis female 87.2 / 89.1), which supports the Slater bar scale (lens-model centre scale would shrink Slater areas by 6-7 %). Root-to-tip L differs (Slater 15.7/16.4 vs Naturalis 16.7-17.3 cm) because the Naturalis preparations keep more shoulder/back feather mass proximally, so L, area/L^2 and AR_wing_only are NOT comparable across the two sources; use the distal planform (primaries, secondaries) for shape.

live_bird_half_span_check.note: (38.2-4.0)/2 = 17.1 cm from the body side to the tip; Naturalis root-to-tip 16.7-17.3 cm is the same; Slater 15.4-15.7 (dorsal) is 8-10 % less (root cut nearer the wrist side or less shoulder mass kept).

ben_gida_2013_bird.note: implied area = span^2/AR; matches published mean chord 6.0 cm (228/38.2 = 5.97)

two_wing_area_from_scans_cm2.published_range_with_body: 230-282 (A-II definitions incl. body between the wings; Ben-Gida implied 228)
two_wing_area_from_scans_cm2.note: 2 x single-wing scan area = 171-178 cm2, i.e. 22-25 % below the published 229-230 cm2 (two wings; body-between-wings included in the A-II numbers, roughly 4 cm x 6 cm = 24 cm2). Likely contributors (not separately tested): the isolated wing is cut at the shoulder so the root region between the joint and the body side is missing (~10-12 cm2 per wing if 2 cm x 5-6 cm), and pressed dried feathers do not fan out as far as in flight. Use the published area as the size target and the scans for shape.

wingspan_over_total_length.basis: 38.2 cm (live bird) / 21 cm (recommended total length); span/length 1.8 (literature ranges 31-44 / 19-23 give 1.4-2.3)

secondary1_over_wing_length.basis: AVONET species means (Secondary1 79.1 / Wing 128.3): the first secondary tip sits at 62 % of the wing length from the wrist

kipps_over_wing_length.basis: AVONET: primaries project 49 mm past the secondaries (38 % of wing length = hand-wing index 38.4)

mean_chord_over_span_live_bird.basis: Ben-Gida: mean chord 6.0 cm, span 38.2 cm (= 1/AR 1/6.4 = 0.156)

scan_two_wing_area_over_published.basis: 2 x Slater 20907 dorsal 85.5 cm2 = 171 vs published 229: scans are ~22-25 % small in area (see notes.md)

primary_projection_study_skins.basis: folded-wing tip sits at 0.94-1.06 of the bill-tip to tail-tip length: the primaries reach about the tail tip
